In [[probability theory]], '''Spitzer's formula''' or '''Spitzer's identity''' gives the joint distribution of partial sums and maximal partial sums of a collection of random variables. The result was first published by [[Frank Spitzer]] in 1956.<ref name="spitzer">{{Cite journal | last1 = Spitzer | first1 = F. | author-link = Frank Spitzer| title = A combinatorial lemma and its application to probability theory | doi = 10.1090/S0002-9947-1956-0079851-X | journal = Transactions of the American Mathematical Society | volume = 82 | issue = 2 | pages = 323–339 | year = 1956 | doi-access = free }}</ref> The formula is regarded as "a stepping stone in the theory of sums of independent random variables".<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Ebrahimi-Fard | first1 = K. | last2 = Guo | first2 = L. | last3 = Kreimer | first3 = D. | doi = 10.1088/0305-4470/37/45/020 | title = Spitzer's identity and the algebraic Birkhoff decomposition in pQFT | journal = Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General | volume = 37 | issue = 45 | pages = 11037 | year = 2004 | arxiv = hep-th/0407082 | bibcode = 2004JPhA...3711037E }}</ref>

==Statement of theorem==

Let <math>X_1,X_2,...</math> be [[independent and identically distributed random variables]] and define the partial sums <math>S_n=X_1 + X_2 + ... + X_n</math>. Define <math>R_n=\text{max}(0,S_1,S_2,...S_n)</math>.  Then<ref name="wendel" />

::<math>\sum_{n=0}^\infty \phi_n(\alpha,\beta)t^n = \exp \left[ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{t^n}{n} \left( u_n (\alpha) + v_n(\beta) -1 \right) \right]</math>

where

::<math>\begin{align}
\phi_n(\alpha,\beta) &= \operatorname E(\exp\left[ i(\alpha R_n + \beta(R_n-S_n)\right])\\
u_n(\alpha) &= \operatorname E(\exp \left[i\alpha S_n^+\right]) \\
v_n(\beta) &= \operatorname E(\exp \left[i \beta S_n^-\right])
\end{align}</math>

and ''S''<sup>±</sup> denotes (|''S''|&nbsp;±&nbsp;''S'')/2.

===Proofs===

The formula was first proved by Spitzer.<ref name="spitzer" /> A short proof was later given by Wendel.<ref name="wendel">{{Cite journal | last1 = Wendel | first1 = James G. | title = Spitzer's formula: A short proof | doi = 10.1090/S0002-9939-1958-0103531-2 | journal = Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society | volume = 9 | issue = 6 | pages = 905–908 | year = 1958 | mr = 0103531 | doi-access = free }}</ref> The formula can be understood in terms of a [[Rota-Baxter algebra]].
